lessons.lesson: Never write 'no earnings event in the window' just because the news note doesn't mention a name. Check the name's own earnings estimate and recent 8-K 2.02 / 10-Q filings in the inputs, and say 'unverified' only if they are truly absent. The News Analyst should cover every symbol on the proposal menu, not only flagged ones, so the Portfolio Manager does not shrink positions for lack of data.

lessons.lesson: Before proposing a buy, check it against the Market Analyst's explicit preferences and say so in the thesis if it reverses one. Do not propose token-sized buys (about 1.5% of equity or less) justified only by asset-class diversification, and set the invalidation far enough from entry (not about 1%) that ordinary daily noise cannot trip it.
evidence: 2026-10-29 VXUS $10 (1.7% of equity): the proposal reversed the Market Analyst's 'prefer US core over international' call (VXUS 21d -2.06%, 63d -1.03% vs SPY +4.39%), was a beta-1.12 equity fund (Implicator: 10% stress loss from -22.84 to -23.96, so no diversification), and its invalidation sat about 0.9% under entry. The Skeptic objected and the PM rejected it. This is a process check from the run files; the rejection's outcome is not graded and is not the evidence.

2026-10-30: the PM cited L4 for standing aside (a buy that keeps a 10% cash buffer would be about $9). Note the PM applied it to token size in general; the lesson itself is about token buys justified only by diversification. The Market Analyst's note also keeps the US-core preference (VXUS 21d -1.54%). Watch that L4 does not become a blanket reason to idle cash.

lessons.lesson: Review every held position on every run, including days with no trade: distance from price to the invalidation, earnings dates now inside the 5-day window versus what the thesis says, and thesis text that has gone stale. Where an invalidation clause is qualitative (e.g. 'exchange failure'), state in the reasoning whether it has tripped, and why. Write the re-anchored level or date into the decision reasoning rather than only flagging it.
evidence: 2026-10-30 IDXX: the 10-20 thesis says earnings (11-02) are outside the 5-day window; the print is now one trading day out, the position fell 4.3% today with no news, and only the Skeptic's objection and the News Analyst's upcoming note brought the stale premise up. The PM did weigh it (stress loss about $3) and held knowingly; the thesis text is still stale.

2026-10-30 CARG: the thesis says earnings 11-05 are outside the window and invalidates on a negative surprise inside five trading days; the company confirmed 11-05 after the close (4 trading days out), so the clause is live on a 5.1% position (News Analyst broken_theses).

2026-10-30 BTC/USD: invalidation includes 'an exchange failure'; the record Binance hack (about $6.3B) arguably meets the wording and the News Analyst asked the PM to say explicitly whether it trips. The PM judged it contained (BTC about -3%, still within the 10% stop at about $75.3k, now about 2% away) but only in a closing review, not as a stated decision step.

2026-10-30 DPZ: invalidation anchored to the wrong close for 8 sessions (see L1); the PM raised it again without changing it. The common pattern across these four is held-position drift found by other agents rather than checked up front. This is a process lesson from the run files; none of these cases is a graded outcome.
